purpose: Rerun of the lab's negative, functional and falsification tests, five streams in parallel, one throwaway kind cluster per stream

experiments.comparison: same pass counts, HTTP statuses and audit reasons; expiry latency min/median/max 4.254/5.308/5.328 s in the previous run

falsification.method: each guard mutated on a scratch copy of src/vending-service; unit level: named Go test baseline/mutated/reverted; live level: mutated image (tag nhi-lab/vending-service:falsify-gN) deployed on the stream's own cluster, negative_tests.py run, clean image restored and the suite rerun

g1_forged_signature.live_reverted: 4/5 then 5/5 after disposing the delegation the mutation minted

g2_empty_attenuation.live_reverted: 4/5 then 5/5 after disposing the scopeless delegation the mutation minted

g4_dispose_grant.live_mutated_status: 200 on the captured JWT after disposal

findings: negative_tests.py: the forged-signature and scope-escalation tests vend with the same child selectors the revocation test uses, so a guard that lets either of them mint leaves the child pod holding two SVIDs and also fails the revocation test (g1 mutated, g1 and g2 first reverted runs)

negative_tests.py: the replay test picks the newest attest/deny audit event without matching chain_id; under g3 it matched the forged-signature event, though the test still failed correctly on the status and reason
under g1 the vend audit event still states the signature was verified; the reason string is fixed text written after the check

results_hygiene.pii_scan: no names, handles, emails, hostname, home or scratch paths
results_hygiene.secret_scan: no private keys or API keys; 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...' matches are the lab's own help text; the one full JWS in verify-core/verify-vending.log is a manifest signature whose x5c holds a public certificate from the deleted throwaway CA
